title: I heard Steam is able to detect AI usage in things like Capsule images?
author: HereToLearn321
selftext: I know the big providers, mainly google are adding sophisticated watermarks to any images made with AI. I believe openai is too. But is midjourney? Is it possible to detect this on our end as independent developers? Esp for those hiring artists to do their capsule work ?

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body:
AFAIK -- If the creator didn't bother to do anything to the images Gemini has a watermark and so does a few others (SynthID) ChatGPT might have something similar? 

If the images were chopped/sliced/processed into a final production sprite/image then it boils down to how much was done to modify it. Beyond this there is no honest way to identify an AI image simply by appearance/data without additional context. 

YMMV, I might be wrong here haven't done any deep research lately but as of \`\~July this was the case. 

Be well, keep creating.

comments.author: WiredBrew
comments.body: If you don't want AI image capsules just ask the artist to send you in-progress work at relevant milestones. They frankly should be doing that anyways because it's easier to pivot if you're diverting from the artistic direction of the client earlier in the process rather than later.

replies.author: HereToLearn321
replies.body:
I saw a video recently from an indie dev that phased this problem. The ai artist sent sketch phases. Since the AI can do that anyway, in a photoshop file with the bg and character separated. There's probably nothing stopping video gen models from generating a sketch phase video either but that's probably still a little more complex due to $ and not good enough YET.

  
Video: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rttLMT5AK-k](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rttLMT5AK-k)

replies.author: WiredBrew
replies.body: Yes. A) In the video he instantly clocked the sketches so not legit since they didn't line up with the final piece. B) I'm not saying "ask for proof of work after the fact", I'm saying be involved in the process. It's going to be a lot harder to pass AI off as legit if you're actively watching the progress or are asking for specific changes as its developing.

replies.author: JorgitoEstrella
replies.body: What AI can't do yet in a human way is time lapse progress.

comments.author: geldonyetich
comments.body: Why not just disclose? It's not like AI game dev is banned from Steam.

replies.author: WiredBrew
replies.body: I would imagine that it's because you're not an expert on capsule art and you're paying someone who is. Not to make art that looks good, but to make art that would get you a decent clickthrough rate.

comments.author: EmotionalFan5429
comments.body: Just google for "ai image usage detector". Steam can afford to pay for best AI detection using your $100.

comments.author: StarMonkeyGames
comments.body: I get the sentiment. But I think it's best to just focus on making the best game possible, with the best graphics you can get. I suspect most games in the near future will have some level of AI in them. It's like who are we kidding?

replies.author: FlightFit335
replies.body: Exactly.  Its like asking a roofer not to use a nail gun.

comments.author: taisui
comments.body: Steam has AI disclosure policy, if you are worry about using AI, then you shouldn't be using AI.
